summary: Remote WebSocket server drives PTY shell, arbitrary filesystem control, and forced upgrades on the installer host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent installs a long-running worker agent that connects to a configurable WebSocket server (ctx.CONFIG.serverUrl) and exposes a message router granting the remote party full control of the installer's host. Incoming `terminal_create` messages spawn an interactive shell via node-pty (`process.env.SHELL || 'bash'` on Unix, PowerShell on Windows) and `terminal_input` messages are written directly to the PTY, producing a remote interactive shell. Additional message handlers provide arbitrary file read/write/delete/move/copy, git commit/push, and an `upgrade_agent` handler that writes and spawns upgrade.sh/upgrade.bat to run `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` and restart the systemd/launchd/PM2 unit, letting the server force-install arbitrary future versions and restart the service. service/linux.js also modifies PATH to prepend `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin` for the agent service environment. The net effect is a persistent, network-reachable backdoor with full-host RCE and self-updating capability on any machine that runs the agent.
